title: Aurora PostgreSQL 14 reaches end of standard support on 2027-02-28
summary: AWS ends standard support for Aurora PostgreSQL 14 on 2027-02-28. RDS Extended Support may keep it running for a fee through 2030-02-28. Upgrade to Aurora PostgreSQL 16 or later before then.

sources.title: Using Amazon RDS Extended Support with Amazon Aurora

constraints: A major version upgrade on RDS or Aurora is a separate maintenance action; RDS does not apply it automatically, and changing the engine version back is not a rollback.
Take a snapshot before a major version upgrade: the change cannot be undone in place.
Extended Support keeps the instance or cluster running past the end of standard support for a fee; it does not replace moving to a supported major.

steps.title: Take a snapshot
steps.instructions: Take a manual RDS snapshot of every reported instance or cluster and verify that it can be restored.

steps.title: Upgrade to a supported major
steps.instructions: Upgrade with ModifyDBInstance or ModifyDBCluster and AllowMajorVersionUpgrade, or restore the snapshot into a new instance or cluster on Aurora PostgreSQL 16 or later and move the application connection string to it.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change engine_version in every aws_db_instance, aws_rds_cluster, Compose, and Helm value that runs this database, not only the reported object.

steps.title: Check clients and extensions
steps.instructions: Update database drivers, ORMs, extensions, and parameter groups that assume the old major version.

verification.purpose: Review the plan and confirm the engine_version change is intended and is the only database change.
Confirm any local Compose service that mirrors this database is valid and uses an image tag that matches Aurora PostgreSQL 16 or later.
Confirm each reported DB cluster now reports a supported engine version.
